answer: Cap recognized identities at a fixed trellis of weight-bearing slots each epoch, say 1500, handed out by sealed-bid auction with every bid burned. A sybil farm wanting many identities must buy many slots in one epoch, and its own bulk demand lifts the clearing price it pays on every slot it takes, so the cost per identity climbs with the number it seeks. Each won slot is stamped as a non-transferable pigment mark on one key, checked at settlement against the committed atlas of that epoch's winners; a mark cannot be resold, split, or pre-aged, so clones can never pool a single slot.
